subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation \u00151 Finex Payments
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finexpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@finexpay.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Intro / discovery 1 reliability and fallbacks

Thanks for taking the time today, Marissa and Jonas. Quick note to confirm the topics we covered and capture a few follow-ups so we don't lose momentum.

High level: Finex is evaluating hosted inference providers to replace an in-house GPU service for transaction categorization and fraud scoring. The main decision criteria for us are reliability during traffic spikes, predictable cost, and controlled graceful degradation during outages.

A few things I want to capture from the call: 
- Our current stack: self-hosted PyTorch models on k8s (GKE), using a mixture of on-demand and preemptible instances. KV cache implemented in Redis.
- Recent incidents: two incidents in Q1 where model serving failed over; one was a regional cloud networking outage (3 hours) that forced failover and increased latency to >3s for critical paths; the other was a spike in requests that caused Redis TTL evictions and stale KV cache hits (30-45 minutes) causing accuracy regressions.
- Success criteria: sub-200ms p95 latency for the majority of user-facing traffic, <1% error/timeout rate in peak hours, and documented fallback behavior that keeps user experience acceptable even when full model capacity is degraded.

Please send a brief recap and next steps (including what you need from our side for a technical deep dive). Also, can you share any SOC2 / security questionnaire responses up front so our security team can start the review?

Best,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Engineering, Finex Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finexpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery 1 reliability and fallbacks

Hi Alex 1 great talking earlier. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, assumptions, and proposed next steps so we can align the technical deep dive.

Recap of pain points and incident history you shared:
- Regional outage (Q1): network problem in one cloud region led to a multi-hour failover. Primary impact was increased latency and some dropped requests when traffic routed to another region.
- Cache eviction event (Q1): Redis TTL settings caused hot keys to be evicted under burst traffic; resulted in stale KV cache hits and lower prediction quality for ~30-45 minutes.
- Concern: you need predictable degradation (graceful fallback) that avoids large accuracy regressions or user-facing errors during incidents.

Current stack & constraints:
- Models: ensemble of transformer-based scoring models (internal variants), served in PyTorch on GKE.
- Cache: Redis for prefix/KV caching; important for latency/throughput.
- Traffic profile: steady baseline with periodic large spikes (marketing pushes).
- Security: must pass SOC2 review and have clear evidence of audit logs and key management.

Success criteria (what Finex needs to be comfortable with):
1) Latency: p95 <= 200ms for core inference path under normal loads.
2) Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime for inference endpoints (we can map to SLA tiers).
3) Degradation behavior: during overload or regional failures, system should degrade to a lower-cost/approx model or serve cached responses with documented accuracy impact (<=5% accuracy delta preferred).
4) Observability: token-level/route-level tracing and incident logs available to your SREs for postmortems.

How Redwood addresses these areas (high level):
- Smart routing + multi-region failover with automated fallback to compatible model variants in another region.
- Prefix/KV caching with configurable TTLs and eviction safeguards; suggestion engine for cache sizing.
- Gradient fallback policies: run a quantized or distilled variant when capacity constrained to keep latency low and degrade accuracy smoothly.
- SLO/SLA mapping we can propose: 99.9% uptime for hosted tiers, with documented escalation and credit policy.

Requested items from Finex before the technical deep dive:
- Example payloads (anonymized) or a small sample trace showing traffic profile (size, token lengths).
- SOC2 questionnaire (if you want us to pre-populate responses we can).
- Confirmation of preferred time for a 60-90 minute technical deep dive with Jonas (infrastructure/routing) and Chloe (customer reliability/ops).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share the SOC2 questionnaire + example payloads (if possible). (Alex)
2) Schedule a technical deep dive next week 1 Jonas suggests Tue/Wed mornings PT. (Marissa)
3) Redwood to prepare a short playbook describing graceful degradation options (fallback model variants, region failover policy, caching defaults) tailored to Finex. (Marissa / Jonas)

If that looks right I can follow up with a calendar invite and attach our SOC2 front-matter and a short incident-playbook draft.

Thanks 1 talk soon.

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finexpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@finexpay.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery 1 reliability and fallbacks

Marissa 1 thanks for the clear recap. Confirmed and a couple of clarifications: 
- We can provide a small, anonymized sample of 10k requests and a traffic profile by end of day tomorrow.
- Attaching our SOC2 questionnaire and the incident summary you asked for (see attachments). The incident_summary_2026Q1.pdf includes timelines and our postmortem notes for both events.

We like the idea of quantized/distilled fallbacks rather than full-deny. A few priorities for the deep dive:
- How Redwood handles cache cold-start during region failover (can we pre-warm or replicate hot keys?)
- Behavior of fallback model variants on latency and accuracy (can Jonas share benchmarks we can compare?)
- How logs/traces are exposed for our SREs (read-only dashboards, S3 export, or direct API?)

I'll accept a calendar invite for Tue morning PT. Also looping in Priya (security lead) 1 she will lead the SOC2 review and will follow up with any gaps.

Thanks,
Alex

Attachments: SOC2-questionnaire.xlsx, incident_summary_2026Q1.pdf

Subject: Re: Intro / discovery 1 reliability and fallbacks

Perfect 1 thanks Alex and Priya. I got the attachments (we'll start pre-filling the SOC2 answers and review the incident doc).

I scheduled a 60-minute technical deep dive for Tue Jun 23, 2026 at 9:30 AM PT and sent a calendar invite to this thread. Jonas will run through routing, cache replication options and a few benchmark slides for fallback models; Chloe will cover ops/observability and SLO-to-SLA mapping.

For the deep dive please send the anonymized request sample and any traffic percentiles (p50/p95/p99) you have 1 that will help Jonas pick the right fallback strategy to demo. If you want us to prepare an initial playbook before the call I can share a short PDF with recommended TTLs, cache sizing heuristics, and suggested fallback model ladder (full model -> quantized -> distilled -> cached responses).

Next steps summary (owned):
- Finex: share anonymized sample + traffic percentiles (Alex) 1 due 2026-06-17 EOD.
- Finex: Priya to start SOC2 review (Priya) 1 link in calendar notes.
- Redwood: pre-fill SOC2 front-matter and produce a 1-page incident/playbook draft (Marissa) 1 will share before the deep dive.

If anything changes on timing let me know. Looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
Marissa
